02. Though, the impugned order is being questioned by the petitioner inter-alia on the grounds that the Court below without affording an opportunity to the prosecution passed the impugned order and awarded lesser punishment to the accused respondents herein than the one prescribed under the Act of 1954, yet upon coming of the petition for consideration today, the appearing counsel for the parties invited the attention of this Court to the judgement passed by the Apex Court in case titled as "Nemi Chand Vs State of Rajasthan" being Criminal Appeal No. 214 of 2016 arising out of SLP (Criminal) No. 2148/2013 dated 10.03.2016 and would submit that the issue is now no more res integra qua the controversy involved in the petition in view of the judgement supra of the Apex Court, whereunder it came to be held that the amendment carried out in the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 by incorporating Section 16A (Section 51 & 52 of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006) providing for levying of fine against the accused persons can be applied in respect of earlier cases as well pending in the Court and that, as such, the imposition of fine only upon the accused respondents herein by the Trial Court would be in tune and line with the judgment of the Apex Case passed in Nemi Chand's case supra.
03.

sentences.text: Having heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the law laid down by the Apex Court in the judgment supra, the instant petition deserves to be settled in terms of the said judgement of the Apex Court.
Accordingly, the petition is disposed of upholding the impugned order 21.05.2008 passed by the Court below.
